identity_snapshot.short_description: A sky-borne civilization of skyships, bonded dragons, and storm-callers, built on the conviction that all true power and loyalty must be freely chosen, sheltered behind the Maelstrom Barrier.
identity_snapshot.civilization_type: Loose confederation of free sky-holds, corsair compacts, and dragon-bonded riders bound by chosen oaths rather than borders.
identity_snapshot.core_belief: Loyalty that is forced is no loyalty at all; the storm and the bond must be entered freely.
primary_corruption_risk: Anti-duty extremism that abandons the bonded
identity_snapshot.domain_stone_or_source: The Storm Core — the Tempest Stone fragment at the eye of the Maelstrom Barrier, resonating through bonded dragons and the wind itself.
identity_snapshot.magic_style: Storm-calling and bond-resonance: wind, lightning, and flight powered by the Core, the Barrier, and freely bonded dragons together.
identity_snapshot.main_magic_cost: Stamina and a share of the self — the storm thins the caster's edges, and the bond demands mutual vulnerability.
identity_snapshot.political_center: Skyhold Aerie, where the Free Skies Assembly convenes among the high roosts.
identity_snapshot.military_identity: Fast, mobile, and improvisational: strike from the wind, never anchor, never be cornered.
identity_snapshot.economic_base: Sky-freight, cloud-markets, salvage, courier networks, and dragon-roost commerce.
identity_snapshot.biggest_internal_conflict: Whether freedom permits forced restraint to save lives (Dragon-Bond Sanctum traditionalists) or whether all restraint is tyranny (Chainbreaker Radicals).
identity_snapshot.biggest_external_threat: Abyss anti-air towers and Void-storms that the weakening Maelstrom Barrier can no longer fully turn aside.
identity_snapshot.keeper_exploit: The Keeper splits Tempest's freedom into control-versus-anti-duty extremism, so the sky-holds fight over what freedom means while the Barrier erodes.
identity_snapshot.void_lie: Love that cannot restrain is love that lets death win.

canon_facts: Tempest shelters behind the Maelstrom Barrier, a vast storm-wall tied to the Storm Core fragment of the fractured pure Nexus Stone.
Dragon bonds are sacred and must be freely chosen by both rider and dragon; forced bonds are a spiritual violation.
Storm magic draws on three sources together — the Storm Core, the Maelstrom Barrier, and bonded dragons.
Tempest has no single ruler; the Free Skies Assembly coordinates the sky-holds by consent.
The Dragon-Bond Sanctum guards bond-law; the Chainbreaker Radicals call all restraint tyranny.
Corsair compacts and cloud-markets make Tempest a trade and salvage power, and a smuggling one.
cannot_contradict: Tempest magic and loyalty must always be freely chosen; forced bonds and forced service are violations.
Tempest corruption must distort freedom into either forced control or anti-duty abandonment, never generic darkness.
Tempest internal politics must respect the Sanctum / Chainbreaker / corsair / Assembly fracture.
The Maelstrom Barrier cannot be commanded by force; it answers to the Core's resonance and freely given storm-song.

metaphysical_role.principle_embodied: Freedom and chosen bond — power and loyalty that mean something only because they were entered freely.
metaphysical_role.nexus_stone_aspect: The Stone's capacity for resonance and willing connection — souls and storms bound by consent rather than chains.
metaphysical_role.soul_flow_shaped: Tempest souls pass freely; bonds carry a thread of self between rider and dragon that survives even death as chosen memory.
metaphysical_role.natural_magic: Storm-calling and bond-resonance: wind, lightning, and flight that strengthen with mutual, freely given trust.
metaphysical_role.when_extreme: Freedom curdles into either the tyranny of 'protective' force or the nihilism of abandoning every duty.
metaphysical_role.keeper_exploits_extremity: The Keeper drives both extremes at once, so Tempest tears itself apart debating freedom while the Barrier that protects it all erodes.

domain_stone.origin: A Tempest Stone fragment cast into the sky during the Nexus shattering, around which the Maelstrom Barrier first formed and the first dragons bonded.
domain_stone.public_knowledge: The Core sustains the Maelstrom Barrier that has kept the Abyss and the Void-storms out for ages.
domain_stone.hidden_truth: The Barrier is thinning where forced bonds and anti-duty desertions have weakened the resonance feeding the Core; Void-storms now slip through the gaps.
failure_symptoms: Dragons refusing roosts near the Core
healing_methods: Communal storm-song to re-resonate the Core
domain_stone.keeper_attack_vector: Encourage forced bonds and mass desertions so the resonance feeding the Barrier collapses.
domain_stone.void_attack_vector: Slip Void-storms through Barrier gaps and offer chained power to those desperate to hold the sky.

soul_flow.healthy_soul_flow_description: Souls pass freely on the wind; a chosen bond keeps a thread of shared self between rider and dragon that endures as honored memory.
soul_flow.damaged_soul_flow_description: Forced bonds trap a thread of self against its will; broken or chained bonds leave both parties hollow, haunting the wind as storm-echoes.
forbidden_soul_processes: Forcing a bond on an unwilling rider or dragon
Severing a bond by force to steal its thread
common_soul_wounds: Riders haunted by a bond broken against their will
soul_flow.keeper_disruption_strategy: Multiply forced bonds and broken ones until the wind is thick with chained storm-echoes.
soul_flow.void_disruption_strategy: Whisper that a forced bond is only love being brave, so the desperate chain what they should free.

true_virtues.name: Freedom
true_virtues.healthy_definition: The right and responsibility to choose one's own bonds, course, and risks.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: No sky-hold conscripts; crews sign on and may leave at port.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A captain frees a pressed crew even when shorthanded for the fight.
true_virtues.political_expression: The Assembly governs by consent and may be left by any sky-hold.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Storm magic answers most strongly to those who command nothing and ask freely.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Corsair compacts are voluntary and dissolvable; no debt-bondage at sea.
true_virtues.military_expression: Soldiers fight as volunteers; a forced soldier is a liability, not an asset.
true_virtues.common_saying: A chained wind is just stale air.

true_virtues.name: Chosen Bond
true_virtues.healthy_definition: Loyalty made sacred precisely because it was entered freely and can be freely kept.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Bond-day is the highest Tempest festival; both parties must speak the choice aloud.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A rider honors a dragon's refusal even at terrible cost.
true_virtues.political_expression: Alliances are oaths between equals, renewed by consent, not inherited.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Bond-resonance grows with mutual, freely given trust.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Partnerships are sealed by chosen word, not coercive contract.
true_virtues.military_expression: A bonded pair outfights any number of conscripts.
true_virtues.common_saying: The bond you choose is the only one that flies.

true_virtues.name: Daring
true_virtues.healthy_definition: The courage to enter the storm and the bond despite their risks.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Stories prize the bold who chose well over the cautious who chose nothing.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A storm-caller rides into the Barrier's gap to seal it.
true_virtues.political_expression: Leaders are those who risked the most for the sky-holds, freely.
true_virtues.magical_expression: The storm rewards those who give themselves to it without grasping.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Salvage fortunes are won by daring the worst weather.
true_virtues.common_saying: The cautious never feel the wind.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: Forcing a bond or restraint on another 'for their own good,' mistaking control for love.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: A crisis makes forcing a restraint the only way to save a life, and it works.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Fear, grief, and the comforting logic that love must sometimes override consent.
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Each forced bond hollows the Barrier's resonance and feeds the chained-echo wound.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: Love that cannot restrain is love that lets death win.
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Tempest becomes a cage that calls itself a sky, and the Barrier fails.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: The belief that every bond, duty, and restraint is tyranny to be shattered, including the ones that protect others.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: Real abuses of forced loyalty make all loyalty look like a chain.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Righteous anger, the thrill of breaking, and recruitment among the abandoned.
who_benefits: Abyss, which profits from Tempest disunity
who_suffers: The bonded who are abandoned mid-flight
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Mass desertion collapses the chosen bonds that feed the Barrier.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: Only the unbound are truly free, even if the sky falls behind them.
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Freedom eats its own foundations; no one holds the line and the Void-storms pour in.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: Reckless self-indulgence that calls itself daring while abandoning all responsibility.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: A daring raider is celebrated and stops distinguishing courage from plunder.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Glory, easy salvage, and crowds that cheer the spectacle.
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Turns Tempest's daring into a reputation for piracy that isolates it.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: Take what the wind allows; the sky owes you.
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Tempest is shunned as a nest of pirates and loses the alliances it needs.

keeper_exploit_pattern.corruption_strategy: Drive freedom into two warring extremes — forced 'protective' control and anti-duty abandonment — so Tempest exhausts itself in the argument while the Barrier's resonance fails.
preferred_crisis_conditions: A Barrier gap and incoming Void-storm
A famous bond broken in public
An Abyss siege forcing hard choices
keeper_exploit_pattern.domain_stone_damage_type: Resonance starvation as chosen bonds are forced or shattered, thinning the Maelstrom Barrier.
keeper_exploit_pattern.common_lie: Freedom means you must choose: cage them or abandon them.
keeper_exploit_pattern.long_term_goal: Collapse the chosen-bond resonance that powers the Barrier, opening the sky to the Void and cracking the prison.

void_temptation_pattern.temptation_phrase: Love that cannot restrain is love that lets death win.
void_temptation_pattern.immediate_benefit: A forced bond or chained storm grants instant control — the dragon obeys, the gap seals, the crew holds.
void_temptation_pattern.hidden_cost: The forced thread festers; the Barrier's resonance thins and a chained echo is born.
void_temptation_pattern.identity_damage: The forcer begins to define safety as control, losing the ability to trust a free choice.
void_temptation_pattern.soul_flow_damage: A thread of self is trapped against its will, hollowing both parties.
void_temptation_pattern.reality_damage: Local storm-song sours; winds answer with Void echoes near the forced bond.
visible_stage_1_symptoms: A dragon obeying with dull eyes
visible_stage_3_symptoms: A chained storm-echo wailing on the wind
A Barrier gap that will not close
The forcer unable to accept any free refusal

magic_systems.source: The Storm Core and the Maelstrom Barrier, drawn through freely given storm-song.
political_use: Maintaining the Barrier as shared defense
civilian_use: Rain for crops on the high roosts
abuse_modes: Chaining a storm to command rather than ask
magic_systems.keeper_corruption_vector: Tempt callers to command the storm instead of asking it.
magic_systems.void_enhancement_vector: Offer chained storm-power that seals the gap now and tears it wider later.

magic_systems.source: The freely chosen bond between rider and dragon, resonating with the Storm Core.
political_use: Bonded pairs as living symbols of chosen loyalty
abuse_modes: Restraining a dragon against its will
Severing a bond to steal its thread
magic_systems.keeper_corruption_vector: Reframe forced restraint as protective love.
magic_systems.void_enhancement_vector: Offer obedience now in exchange for a hollowed, chained thread later.

magic_costs.description: Riding the storm thins the caller's edges; give too much and the self disperses into the wind.
magic_costs.minor_effect: Lightheaded exhilaration, a blurred hour after.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Lasting fogginess of self; the caller feels 'spread thin.'
magic_costs.severe_effect: Identity dissolution into the storm; the caller is lost to the wind.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Grounding at a roost, a bond's anchoring thread, communal storm-song.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Identity fracture the Void can mimic with a storm-echo.

magic_costs.description: A chosen bond is a vow of mutual vulnerability that both parties carry.
magic_costs.minor_effect: The felt presence of another's trust.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Shared pain and risk; one's wounds are partly the other's.
magic_costs.severe_effect: If a bond is forced or broken, the weight becomes a hollowing wound.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Honoring or freely releasing the bond; wind-burial if a partner falls.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Forced-bond hollowing exploited into a chained storm-echo.

magic_costs.description: Commanding rather than asking the storm overdraws the Storm Core and thins the Barrier.
magic_costs.minor_effect: A flicker in the Maelstrom Barrier.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: A local Barrier gap; Void-storms test the seam.
magic_costs.severe_effect: A persistent gap and a chained-echo wound near the overdraw.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Cease commanding, restore free storm-song, mend forced bonds.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Barrier collapse if strain compounds across sky-holds.

government.government_type: Voluntary confederation of sky-holds and compacts coordinated by an assembly of consent.
government.ruling_body: The Free Skies Assembly, convened at Skyhold Aerie.
government.religious_authority: The Dragon-Bond Sanctum interprets bond-law and storm-song doctrine.
government.military_authority: The Galewardens, a volunteer skyship navy answerable to the Assembly.
government.economic_authority: The Cloud-Market Compact of corsair captains and freight guilds.
government.magical_authority: The Eye Vigil maintains the Barrier; the Sanctum governs bonds.
government.succession_or_selection_method: Assembly seats are delegated by each sky-hold and revocable at will; no seat is inherited or held by force.
government.legitimacy_source: The freely given consent of the sky-holds and the integrity of the Barrier.
known_cracks_in_legitimacy: The Assembly cannot compel sky-holds, so crises stall
Corsair compacts pursue profit over defense
emergency_powers: Temporary Galewarden levy by volunteer call
corruption_vulnerabilities: The Protective Chain in a crisis

class_structure.description: Those who share a freely chosen bond with a dragon; living symbols of Tempest's creed.
burdens: Held to the strictest consent ethics
class_structure.military_obligation: Volunteer; a bonded pair is courted, never conscripted.
class_structure.political_voice: High within the Sanctum and Assembly.
common_grievances: Made into symbols rather than persons

class_structure.description: Crews, couriers, salvagers, roost-keepers, and the unbonded many.
burdens: Exposed to Barrier breaches and raids
class_structure.economic_role: The body of sky-freight, salvage, and markets.
common_grievances: Dragon elites preach freedom while monopolizing prestige
Left exposed when the Barrier thins

class_structure.description: Independent operators of compacts, salvage fleets, and cloud-markets.
burdens: No safety net outside the compact
class_structure.economic_role: Backbone of trade, salvage, and smuggling.
common_grievances: Blamed for license they did not commit
Pressured by both Sanctum ethics and Chainbreaker zeal

trade_routes: The High Lanes above the domains
Corsair salvage runs along the Barrier
black_market_goods: Smuggled corrupted sap and overcharge relics
economy.wartime_economy_behavior: Shifts to fast freight and salvage of war-wrecks; corsairs profiteer unless bound by compact ethics.
famine_or_shortage_risks: Barrier breach disrupting the High Lanes
economy.keeper_attack_vector: Choke food and skymetal imports so sky-holds turn to license and forced control to survive.

military_doctrine.strategic_identity: Strike from the storm, never anchor, never be cornered; speed and surprise over mass.
preferred_battlefield: Barrier seams where enemies cannot follow
military_doctrine.defensive_strategy: Use the Barrier and the storm as a moving wall; refuse fixed positions.
military_doctrine.offensive_strategy: Lightning raids and aerial dominance, then vanish before counterattack.
military_doctrine.logistics_strategy: Fast freight and salvage; vulnerable to food and skymetal shortages.
military_doctrine.intelligence_strategy: Courier knots and storm-sense scouting; weak to Abyss anti-air ambush.
desperate_tactics: Forced bonds to hold the line
Overdrawing the Core to seal a breach
common_weaknesses: Dependence on imports and the Barrier
military_doctrine.keeper_exploit: Force a choice between chaining dragons and abandoning the line.
military_doctrine.void_escalation: Offer chained storms that win the breach and widen it.

warfront_behavior.negotiation_style: Informal, equal-to-equal, and allergic to anything resembling compulsion.
betrayal_conditions: An ally demands conscription or forced bonds
alliance_conditions: A shared Void/Abyss threat to the sky
Respect for chosen bond and free passage
warfront_behavior.occupation_style: Tempest rarely occupies; it raids and withdraws, mistrusting any hold it must garrison.
warfront_behavior.resistance_style: Endless mobile harassment; impossible to pin, easy to fracture from within.

major_locations.name: Skyhold Aerie
major_locations.location_type: High capital roost and seat of the Assembly
major_locations.description: A cluster of wind-carved spires and dragon roosts wreathed in the inner Maelstrom, where the Free Skies Assembly convenes.
major_locations.political_function: Seat of the Free Skies Assembly and bond-law arbitration.
major_locations.magical_function: Strongest tap of the Storm Core's resonance and the Eye Vigil.
major_locations.military_function: Galewarden muster point and bonded-rider roost.
major_locations.spiritual_function: Heart of bond-day rites and storm-song.
major_locations.civilian_function: Free port for crews, couriers, and salvagers.
known_secrets: The Eye Vigil quietly tracks growing Barrier gaps it has not announced
major_locations.keeper_attack_vector: Let the Sanctum–Chainbreaker quarrel paralyze the Assembly while Barrier gaps widen.
void_symptoms: A second voice under the storm-song
Bonds fraying near the inner Maelstrom
quest_hooks: Expose or address the hidden Barrier gaps
Mediate the bond-law dispute tearing the Assembly

major_locations.name: The Tornwatch Gap
major_locations.location_type: Frontier Barrier-seam fortress facing the Abyss
major_locations.description: A storm-lashed string of roosts guarding a thinning seam in the Maelstrom Barrier, ringed by Abyss anti-air towers.
major_locations.economic_function: Salvage of war-wrecks and forward depot.
major_locations.spiritual_function: Where chained storm-echoes are most heard.
contested_by: Frightened riders tempted to force bonds
known_secrets: Some wardens have used forced bonds to hold the seam
major_locations.keeper_attack_vector: Corner the wardens into chaining dragons to seal the gap.
void_symptoms: A gap that will not close
quest_hooks: Seal the Tornwatch gap without forcing a bond
Decide what to do about wardens who chained their dragons

culture.daily_life_summary: Life is lived between roost and sky, measured by tides of wind and market; nothing is owned that cannot be left, and every bond is a choice spoken aloud.
culture.family_customs: Kinship is by chosen oath as much as blood; crews become families and may part freely.
culture.love_and_marriage_customs: Partners exchange a storm-song they composed; either may release the bond, which is honored, not shamed.
culture.education_system: Children apprentice to crews and roosts; the first lesson is that no one may chain them and they may chain no one.
culture.work_and_apprenticeship: Sign-on apprenticeships, dissolvable at any port; mastery is proven by daring and trust earned.
culture.food_and_market_life: Imported grains, salvaged delicacies, and storm-brewed spirits; cloud-markets float and scatter with the weather.
culture.funeral_or_death_customs: Wind-burial releases the freely fallen to the sky; a bonded partner sings the last storm-song.
public_honors: The Free Wind (for a great free choice)
A storm-song kept in the roost-courts
common_sayings: A chained wind is just stale air.
The bond you choose is the only one that flies.
Leave clean or do not leave at all.
children_common_beliefs: The wind remembers a freely given name
A forced bond curdles the storm
Dragons can hear a lie in your choice
class_differences: Bonded riders revered; skyfolk free but un-prestiged

religion.central_belief: The storm and the bond are sacred only when freely entered; consent is the holiest law of the sky.
sacred_symbols: The open hand and the dragon
common_prayers_or_oaths: I choose, and I may unchoose.
Let the wind take what it is freely given.
heresies: The Protective Chain creed (forced bonds as love)
sacred_taboos: Chaining a storm or a soul
Severing a bond to steal its thread
religion.relationship_to_death: Death is a release to the free wind; a chained death is the true horror.
religion.relationship_to_sacrifice: Sacrifice must be freely chosen, never demanded; a forced sacrifice is a chain.
religion.relationship_to_memory: Memory rides the wind as freely given song; forced memory festers.
religion.relationship_to_truth: A choice made under coercion is a lie; truth lives only where consent does.
religion.keeper_corruption_strategy: Promote both the Protective Chain and Chainbreaker heresies until the sky has no center.
religion.void_false_revelation_style: A thrilling storm-vision that to truly love is to seize and hold.

factions.power_base: Economic control of trade and salvage.
factions.player_use: Source of ships, smuggling, and grey deals.

factions.power_base: Righteous zeal and recruitment of the disaffected.

factions.player_use: Populist allies and a bridge between elite and common.

external_relations.void_exploit: Offer chained storms that hold the gap and widen it.

internal_power_struggles.title: The Tornwatch Restraint
internal_power_struggles.issue: Whether dragons may be forcibly restrained to seal Barrier breaches during the Abyss siege.
internal_power_struggles.public_argument: Cornered wardens: 'A chained dragon is better than a fallen sky.' The Sanctum: 'A forced bond rots the very resonance that holds the Barrier.'
internal_power_struggles.hidden_argument: Some wardens already force bonds in secret; Chainbreakers want the scandal to discredit all bond authority.
possible_player_sides: Permit emergency restraint to hold the seam
Find a free-bond or storm-song method to seal it without force
internal_power_struggles.keeper_best_outcome: Forced restraint becomes normal doctrine and the resonance collapses.
internal_power_struggles.void_best_outcome: Chained storms hold the gaps while the Barrier quietly fails.
internal_power_struggles.peaceful_resolution: A Sanctum-supervised ban on forced bonds plus a volunteer surge and storm-song reinforcement of the seam.
internal_power_struggles.violent_resolution: Chainbreakers and wardens clash at Tornwatch as a breach opens.
internal_power_struggles.third_order_effect: Bonded riders split; unbonded crews accuse the elite of hypocrisy; corsairs sell anti-bond tools.
internal_power_struggles.fifth_order_effect: The Keeper benefits as Tempest freedom fractures into control versus anti-duty extremism.

rumor_weaponization_methods: Inflating a restraint into mass tyranny
rumor_mutation_patterns: 'Restrained a dragon to save it' becomes 'enslaves dragons'
A sealed breach becomes 'the Barrier is failing everywhere'

trust_is_built_by: Honoring a refusal at real cost
Keeping a bond freely without grasping
enemies_become_tolerable_when: They free a chained soul at cost
They defend the Barrier without compulsion
allies_become_suspect_when: They preach that all bonds are chains
romance_conflicts: A Sanctum lover who cannot forgive a coercive choice
A Chainbreaker lover who scorns the player's kept bonds
betrayal_triggers: Forcing a bond on the player's ally
Selling a crew to the Abyss
forgiveness_conditions: Bearing the storm-thinning to seal what one broke
permanent_enemy_conditions: Selling the sky to the Void for control

if_then_because_examples.if: The player forces a dragon to obey during a crisis
if_then_because_examples.because: Tempest considers forced loyalty a spiritual violation even when the result saves lives.

if_then_because_examples.if: A former enemy frees a chained crew at real cost
if_then_because_examples.then: Tempest may downgrade them from enemy to uneasy partner
if_then_because_examples.because: Honoring freedom proves character more deeply than past allegiance.

if_then_because_examples.if: A rider restrains their injured dragon to save it from a Void-storm
if_then_because_examples.then: Dragon trust falls sharply even though the dragon survives
if_then_because_examples.because: Life preserved by violating chosen bond is still a violation of the bond.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player honors a dragon's refusal despite great cost
if_then_because_examples.then: Sanctum and dragon trust rise sharply
if_then_because_examples.because: Respecting refusal is the truest proof of Tempest's creed.

if_then_because_examples.if: A captain abandons their bonded post mid-crisis on principle
if_then_because_examples.then: Even Chainbreaker sympathizers grow wary of relying on them
if_then_because_examples.because: Freedom that abandons the dependent reads as nihilism, not liberty.

if_then_because_examples.if: Wardens are exposed forcing bonds to hold a Barrier seam
if_then_because_examples.then: Bonded riders split and unbonded crews cry hypocrisy
if_then_because_examples.because: The elite preaching freedom while chaining dragons fractures the whole creed.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player seals a Barrier gap by storm-song instead of force
if_then_because_examples.then: Eye Vigil and Assembly trust rise
if_then_because_examples.because: Asking the storm rather than commanding it honors the Core's resonance.

if_then_because_examples.if: A corsair raids an ally under the banner of free daring
if_then_because_examples.then: Tempest's alliances and Compact standing suffer
if_then_because_examples.because: License dressed as freedom isolates Tempest from the partners it needs.

if_then_because_examples.if: A Radiance ally forces service on a free Tempest crew
if_then_because_examples.then: Tempest shifts them toward declared enemy
if_then_because_examples.because: Forced loyalty is the one violation Tempest cannot forgive.

if_then_because_examples.if: The player submits a contested bond decision to a roost-court
if_then_because_examples.then: Tempest factions grant more latitude on the result
if_then_because_examples.because: Letting the community judge consent honors freedom over private command.

if_then_because_examples.if: A grieving rider is talked back from forcing a bond
if_then_because_examples.then: The Sanctum's trust in the player deepens
if_then_because_examples.because: Preventing a forced bond heals a wound before it festers into a chained echo.

starting_bonuses: Reputation for keeping your word among skyfolk
starting_burdens: No safety net outside chosen bonds
Pressure to prove you force nothing
starting_faction_assumptions: Watched by the Sanctum for any coercion
Tempted by the Chainbreakers if you have been wronged
common_npc_reactions: Hostility if you force a bond
unique_origin_questions: What bond have you chosen, and could you release it?
Have you ever forced loyalty to save a life?
Is the Barrier worth a single chain?
possible_dark_secret_options: You once forced a bond to survive and hid it
You abandoned a crew on principle and they died

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player helps a rider forcibly restrain their injured dragon to keep it from flying into a lethal Void-storm.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Tempest sees life preserved by violating chosen bond — a real rescue that is also a real transgression.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: The Dragon-Bond Sanctum hears of the restraint and is alarmed; Chainbreaker Radicals weaponize the story; Kaida questions the player's understanding of freedom.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Rider gratitude +15; dragon trust -20; Tempest bond-law stress +8.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: The Sanctum opens a bond-law inquiry; Chainbreakers spread the tale; Kaida confronts the player.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Bonded riders split over emergency restraint; unbonded commoners accuse the elite of hypocrisy; corsairs sell anti-bond restraint tools.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: A sky-alliance mission is delayed; Azyr refuses to fly under commanders who tolerate forced loyalty; Abyss anti-air towers gain time to fortify.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper benefits because Tempest freedom fractures into control versus anti-duty extremism.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Tempest's resonance frays as the bond-law schism deepens.
cause_effect_examples.void_gain: The Void whispers, 'Love that cannot restrain is love that lets death win.'
player_intervention_options: Submit to a Dragon-Bond trial
Give the dragon public voice
Find a healing method that restores consent
Expose Chainbreaker exaggeration
Help the rider apologize and release control

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player seals a thinning Tornwatch Barrier gap by leading a volunteer storm-song instead of chaining a dragon to do it.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Tempest sees the creed vindicated: the storm was asked, not commanded.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: The Eye Vigil and Sanctum are heartened; cornered wardens are relieved; Chainbreakers lose a grievance.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The gap closes and the Void-storm is turned aside.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Barrier integrity +10; Eye Vigil trust +12; the player gains standing among bonded riders.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Wardens who had forced bonds reconsider; a volunteer surge forms.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Storm-song reinforcement spreads to other seams; forced-bond temptation drops at the front.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: The Assembly funds a Barrier-renewal vigil; Abyss loses its easiest breach.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper's resonance-starvation strategy is set back as chosen bonds re-strengthen the Core.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Reduced — unless exhaustion makes the next seam fall to force.
player_intervention_options: Train more storm-song cantors
Publicly credit the volunteers, not yourself
Help wardens release earlier forced bonds
Press the Assembly for sustained Barrier funding

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player exposes Tornwatch wardens who secretly chained their dragons to hold the seam.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Tempest is forced to weigh the sanctity of consent against the wardens' desperate success.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: The Sanctum is vindicated; the wardens are shamed; Chainbreakers seize the scandal; the Assembly panics about the front.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The forced bonds are documented and made public.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Sanctum trust +10; frontier morale -8; the chained dragons' trust must be rebuilt.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Chainbreaker recruitment spikes; the wardens face a roost-court; chained-echo wounds are discovered.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: A debate erupts over whether the seam can be held without force; storm-song reinforcement is attempted.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Bond-law is reaffirmed with oversight, slowing brute-force defense but healing resonance.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Maelstrom's resonance stabilizes slightly, denying the Keeper a quiet win.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Conditional: large if the morale drop opens a breach, small if storm-song fills the gap.
player_intervention_options: Offer the wardens a path to atone by releasing the bonds
Lead a storm-song to replace the forced restraint
Shield whistleblowers from Chainbreaker exploitation
Help the chained dragons heal and choose

cause_effect_examples.root_event: A corsair captain under the player's banner raids a Sanctuary supply convoy, calling it free daring.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Tempest splits on whether this is bold salvage or license that shames the creed.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: The Compact is divided; the Sanctum condemns license; Sanctuary brands all Tempest as pirates.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Short-term loot +; Sanctuary trust -15; Tempest reputation for piracy +.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Sanctuary detains other free crews in reprisal; the Compact debates expelling the captain.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Cross-domain trade tightens; the High Lanes near Sanctuary grow dangerous.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: A needed anti-Abyss accord with Sanctuary stalls over the raid.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper benefits as Tempest is isolated and an alliance against the Abyss collapses.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Tempest loses the partners it needs against the Void.
player_intervention_options: Return the plunder and discipline the captain
Distinguish daring from license publicly
Broker reparations with Sanctuary
Expel the captain from the compact

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player talks a grieving captain out of forcing a bond on a frightened young dragon to 'protect' it.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Tempest sees a forced-bond wound prevented before it could fester.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: The Sanctum is grateful; Chainbreakers lose a future grievance; the captain is shaken but freed of a terrible choice.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: No bond is forced; the dragon is given space to choose.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Sanctum trust +8; the captain's respect for the player +10; a potential chained-echo averted.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: The dragon, unforced, may later choose the bond freely; the captain begins to grieve cleanly.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: The story spreads as a counter-narrative to the Protective Chain creed.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Frontier riders gain a model for holding the line without force.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper's forced-bond strategy loses ground as chosen bonds are reaffirmed.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Reduced; a wound that never opened.
player_intervention_options: Help the captain wind-bury their earlier loss
Mentor the young dragon toward a free choice
Share the story to counter the Protective Chain
Pair the captain with a Sanctum bond-elder

metaphysical: In what proportion does storm magic draw on the Core, the Barrier, and bonded dragons — and what happens if one source fails?
Can a chained-echo soul ever be freed, or only wind-buried?
political: Can a consent-only Assembly survive threats that demand fast, binding action?
Is the Unbonded League a reform movement or a Chainbreaker pipeline?
magic: Is there any bounded, ethical emergency restraint, or is all forced bonding a slope?
Can the Barrier be rebuilt once a seam fully fails?
faction: Are the Chainbreakers redeemable reformers or nihilists the Keeper steers?
How many wardens have already forced bonds in secret?
npc: Will Kaida stay the creed's conscience or break under frontier pressure?
Can Azyr be persuaded to a free bond, and with whom?
war_economy: How long can the sky-holds last if food and skymetal imports are cut?
What does a sustained Barrier breach do to the cloud-market economy?
implementation: Should forced bonds be a Void temptation event, a soul-flow wound, and a Barrier (domain-stone) strain at once?
How is a dragon modeled — as an NPC, a bonded relic-like entity, or a unique actor type with its own consent state?

locked_decisions: Tempest magic and loyalty must always be freely chosen; forced bonds and forced service are violations.
Tempest corruption must distort freedom into either the Protective Chain (forced control) or Chainbreaker nihilism (anti-duty abandonment), never generic darkness.
Tempest internal politics must respect the Sanctum / Chainbreaker / corsair / Assembly fracture.
Forcing a bond, chaining a dragon, or severing a bond by force is the violation Tempest cannot forgive.
Storm magic draws on the Storm Core, the Maelstrom Barrier, and bonded dragons together; commanding rather than asking strains all three.
A freely honored refusal is the highest proof of Tempest's creed.
